hints: Look at what each axis and each curve tells you. Which points are on the low CO2 curve and which have high percentage saturation with oxygen?
Remember when haemoglobinic acid (HHb) forms: deoxyhaemoglobin picks up H+ ions from carbonic acid. So ask yourself, when is haemoglobin most loaded with oxygen and least exposed to H+?
walkthrough:
**Recall what haemoglobinic acid is**

Think of it simply. When CO2 is high, more H+ ions are made in the red cell.

Deoxyhaemoglobin mops up those H+ ions to form haemoglobinic acid:
$$Hb + H^+ \rightarrow HHb$$

**Work out when HHb will be lowest**

You want the opposite conditions. Least H+ available and least deoxyhaemoglobin to bind it.

That means low partial pressure of CO2 and high percentage saturation with oxygen (mostly oxyhaemoglobin, $HbO_2$).

**Read the graph and pick the point**

The upper curve is low CO2 partial pressure, so A and C beat B and D for low H+.

Of A and C, C is much higher up the y-axis, so it has far higher oxygen saturation. High saturation plus low CO2 gives the lowest $HHb$, so C is the answer.

options.A: A is on the low CO2 curve which helps, but saturation is low so much haemoglobin is deoxyhaemoglobin ready to form HHb.
options.B: B has both low oxygen saturation and high CO2, so lots of H+ and lots of deoxyhaemoglobin gives high HHb.
options.C: C combines low CO2 (few H+ ions) with very high oxygen saturation (mostly oxyhaemoglobin), so least HHb forms.
options.D: D has high oxygen saturation which helps, but it is on the high CO2 curve so more H+ is present than at C.
